entries.title: In-person events: approve seat requests by organization, or from Slack
entries.summary: Decide a whole team's seat requests at once from **Guests → By organization**, with an optional **Seats per organization** limit. Or post requests to a Slack channel with **Approve**, **Waitlist** and **Decline** buttons; each decision records who made it and when.

where.path: Events → an in-person event → Guests → By organization; Settings → Slack approvals

entries.use_case: Teams that hand-pick a balanced room can approve or cap a whole company in one step, and the people who approve can do it from Slack without opening Sessionboard.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer approves seat requests one by one, wants to limit seats per company, or asks for approvals in Slack.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers running in-person events or tours (dinners, workshops, roadshows).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → an in-person event → an in-person event → Guests → By organization; Settings → Slack approvals
internal.gotchas: Slack decisions need a Sessionboard account in the organization with the same email as in Slack. A Slack workspace already connected to another Sessionboard organization can be connected again for seat requests only; commands and mentions stay with the first organization.
internal.talk_track: Group the requests by company, approve the team in one click, or let your approvers decide right in Slack.

entries.title: In-person events: the packet in reminders, sign-up sources, moments and the after-event loop
entries.summary: Upload a packet and fill in **Getting there** so confirmation and reminder emails carry them; make a tracked sign-up link per channel and person and see sign-ups by source; get a note when the details change, the event is 80% full or it has ended; and send a thank-you with a Survey link or a no-show follow-up after the event.

where.path: Events → an in-person event → Settings → Know before you go; Follow-up

entries.use_case: Guests arrive knowing how to get there, the team sees which channel and which person filled the room, and nobody forgets the follow-up.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to send directions or a PDF to guests, which post brought sign-ups, or how to follow up after an in-person event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers running in-person events or tours (dinners, workshops, roadshows).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → an in-person event → an in-person event → Settings → Know before you go; Follow-up
internal.gotchas: Customized confirmation or reminder emails keep their words: add {{packet_url}} and {{#getting_there}} to them. Moment notes only suggest next steps; nothing is sent without a yes.
internal.talk_track: Send the packet in the reminders, know where each sign-up came from, and close the loop after the event.

entries.title: Scout Agent plans: run a plan that targets sponsors
entries.summary: The Scout Agent plan wizard and the **Run** button now accept plans with **Sponsors** turned on as a target, in addition to **Speakers**. A plan with only **Exhibitors** enabled is still blocked, and the wizard shows the message "Scout Agent can run with Speakers or Sponsors turned on — Exhibitors are not supported yet."

where.path: Prospects → Scout Plans → plan wizard → Targets step (or Run button on a plan)

entries.use_case: Teams that use Scout to find potential sponsors can now create a plan with the Sponsors target enabled and run it directly, without needing a Speakers target on the same plan. This lets sponsorship teams run automated prospect discovery independently of the speaker pipeline.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks whether Scout can find sponsor prospects, or when they have a sponsorship team that wants to use Scout independently of the speaker team.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer already using Scout Agent plans who also manages sponsor prospecting.
internal.staff_path: Prospects → Scout Plans → create or open a plan → Targets step → enable Sponsors
internal.gotchas: A plan with only Exhibitors enabled will still be blocked at the wizard's Targets and Review steps and the Run button will be disabled. The round results view does not yet show per-target outcomes (speaker vs. sponsor); a round where one target succeeds and the other fails shows as a plain Completed. A follow-up PR will add per-target status and error display.
internal.talk_track: Scout can now run a plan that targets sponsors, not just speakers — so your sponsorship team can use the same automated prospecting workflow your speaker team already relies on.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that Scout plans support a Sponsors target, how to enable it in the wizard, and that Exhibitors are saved but not yet runnable.
draft.why_use_it: Scout Agent plans let you define criteria, look-alike accounts and qualifying questions for the types of people or companies you want to find, then run the agent to surface ranked candidates automatically. Use it when you want to build a pipeline of speakers, sponsors or both without manually searching your CRM or the web for every prospect.

entries.title: Embeds: speaker bios and rich-text fields strip unsafe HTML
entries.summary: Speaker bios and rich-text field values rendered in agenda and speaker embeds now pass through a client-side HTML sanitizer. Scripts, iframes, inline `style` attributes, SVG, and other unsafe markup are removed before display. Text, bold, lists, links, and tables render as before.

where.path: Sessions → Embeds → agenda or speaker embed on your website

entries.use_case: Any organizer embedding a speaker list or agenda on their own website benefits automatically: bios and rich-text fields that previously could carry unsafe markup are now sanitized in the widget before rendering, protecting visitors on the organizer's site.

cs_action.note: Inline styles (colour, text-alignment) set by speakers in non-WYSIWYG bio fields will no longer render in embeds. Customers who relied on styled bios in widgets may notice the change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that colour or alignment styling in speaker bios has disappeared from their embedded agenda or speaker list, or asks about a security patch to embeds.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using agenda or speaker embeds on their own website, especially those whose speakers enter rich bios.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Embeds → preview the embed on the customer's website
internal.gotchas: Inline style attributes (e.g. font colour, text-align) are stripped by the new sanitizer. Iframes embedded in bios are also removed. Legitimate bold, lists, links and tables are unaffected. The server-side API was patched in a companion PR and also sanitizes on read.
internal.talk_track: A security fix now sanitizes speaker bios and rich-text fields inside your embedded widgets before they reach your visitors' browsers. Formatting like bold and links is preserved; inline colour styles and iframes are removed.

draft.docs_gap: The embeds guide should note that speaker bios and rich-text field values are sanitized client-side in the widget, and that inline styles (colour, alignment) and iframes set outside the WYSIWYG editor will not render.

entries.title: Advanced Search: browse the global sponsors catalog and add to pipeline
entries.summary: A new **Sponsor Search** page under **Advanced Search** lets organizers browse a global sponsors catalog populated by Sponsor Scout. The table shows company logo, name, domain, industry, HQ country, events attended, and highest sponsorship tier. Clicking a row opens a detail panel with description, website, LinkedIn, and a full **Sponsorships seen** history. The **Add to pipeline** button adds the sponsor to the org's CRM pipeline (idempotent; requires prospects create permission).

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Advanced Search; then Organization → Advanced Search → Sponsors

entries.use_case: Sponsorship teams can search a pre-researched global catalog of sponsors — filtered by tier, industry, HQ country, or events attended — and add promising companies directly to their pipeline without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: The advanced_search feature flag must be on for the org; the sidebar leaf is served from the API nav.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to find new sponsors or build a prospect list without manual research.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs actively prospecting for sponsors who have the Advanced Search feature enabled.
internal.gotchas: Add to pipeline requires the org.prospects create permission; users without it will see a 403. The catalog only shows fields with ≥ 7/10 data coverage — no company size, signals, or contacts.
internal.talk_track: With Sponsor Search you can browse a global catalog of companies that have sponsored events, filter by industry or tier, review their sponsorship history, and add them to your pipeline — all without leaving Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The advanced search guide covers keyword search and segments for contacts but does not mention the Sponsors catalog, its filters, the detail panel, or the Add to pipeline action — all of which should be documented.
draft.why_use_it: Sponsor Search gives you a searchable, pre-researched catalog of companies that have sponsored events, so you can identify and qualify prospects before reaching out. Filter by industry, tier, HQ country, or events attended, then open a company's detail panel to review its sponsorship history, published package prices, and contact links. When a company looks right, add it to your pipeline in one click.

entries.title: Shows: recording slot, episode scheduled time and meeting link now visible
entries.summary: The **Shows** panel now displays the full recording schedule in the show header — for example "Weekly · Tuesday 2:00 PM (America/New_York)" — instead of only "Weekly". Each episode row also shows its scheduled time (converted to the viewer's time zone) and a **Meeting link** button when one is set.
entries.use_case: Show producers who set a weekly recording slot and meeting link can now confirm those details at a glance in the Shows panel, without having to open each episode separately.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says their show's recording schedule or meeting link is missing from the Shows panel.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Shows feature in Sessionboard Marketing.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Content → Shows → open a show
internal.gotchas: The show's wall-clock time is displayed in the show's own time zone (e.g. America/New_York), not shifted to the viewer's zone; episode times are shown in the viewer's local zone.
internal.talk_track: The recording slot and meeting link you set on a show now appear directly in the panel so your team always knows when and where to record.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that the show header displays the full recording schedule (weekday and wall-clock time with time zone) and that each episode row shows the scheduled time in the viewer's zone plus a Meeting link.

entries.title: Agent-built pages: empty-state fallback and designed fonts now display correctly
entries.summary: On pages built by the AI agent, a **data source** with no rows now shows the template's fallback content (the empty state) instead of rendering a blank card. Separately, Google Fonts loaded with `display=swap` now render in the chosen typeface from first paint; previously the compile step forced every font to `display=optional`, so designed fonts never appeared during a visit.
entries.use_case: Organizers who publish agent-built show or program pages before all content is ready will now see a designed empty state instead of a blank card. Attendees visiting those pages will also see the correct brand fonts immediately rather than falling back to system fonts for the entire visit.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports blank cards or wrong fonts on an agent-built page, especially a show or program page with no episodes yet.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the AI agent to build public-facing program or show pages.
internal.gotchas: Templates that handle their own empty state (using sb-unless or sb-if/sb-unless on count) continue to render normally — the fallback only fires when the template has no such check.
internal.talk_track: If your agent-built page showed blank cards when content wasn't ready yet, or if your brand fonts weren't showing up, both are now fixed automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The agents overview guide should note that agent-built pages show a designed fallback when a data source has no rows, and that Google Fonts with display=swap are preserved so brand typography renders from first paint.

entries.title: Webinar results and follow-ups email: automatic post-webinar digest for Marketing
entries.summary: After a self-serve Marketing webinar ends, the webinar owner and hosts automatically receive a **Results and follow-ups** email summarising attendance numbers, open questions, clip count and up to three suggested next actions (such as tagging attendees as prospects or adding them to a pipeline). Each suggestion appears as an **Approval** in the Marketing agent panel, where it can be applied or dismissed within 14 days.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Moment Digests; then Marketing → Webinars → [webinar] → Results

entries.use_case: After a webinar wraps, the owner and hosts get a single email with the key numbers and a short action plan — no manual digging through reports. Suggested CRM actions (tagging prospects, adding to a pipeline) are one click to approve, so follow-up happens while the event is still fresh.

cs_action.note: The MOMENT_DIGESTS flag is off by default. Enable it per org. A dry-run mode (MOMENT_DIGESTS_MODE=dry_run) builds and stores approvals but sends no email — useful for previewing before going live with a customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Marketing webinar customer asks how to follow up with attendees or wants a post-event summary without building a report.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve Marketing customers running webinars with at least 5 attendees on Zoom, Goldcast, ON24, GoTo Webinar, Webex, Microsoft Teams, or BigMarker.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Webinars → [webinar] → Results (after flag is on)
internal.gotchas: Digests are self-serve only — Platform events get a not_self_serve skip recorded and no email is sent. The email is skipped if the webinar is older than 7 days or has fewer than 5 attendees. The 'tag as Hot' suggestion from the spec is not built; tagging marks people as prospects instead. Task-based follow-up for open questions is not built (Tasks are Platform-only). The per-product email preference UI (slice 4) is not yet shipped; the existing 'Emails from Sessionboard' opt-out is honoured in the meantime.
internal.talk_track: Right after your webinar finishes, you'll get an email with your numbers and a short list of suggested actions — tag your hottest attendees as prospects, add them to a pipeline — and you can approve each one with a single click.

draft.docs_gap: The linked guide should document when the email arrives, who receives it, what each section of the email contains (stats, suggested updates, next step, action items), how to act on the Approval suggestions, how to turn the digest off, and the skip conditions (too old, too small, opted out).
draft.why_use_it: The results email lands in your inbox automatically once your webinar data is ready, giving you attendance totals, open questions, clip count and a ranked list of follow-up actions. Each suggested action — such as tagging attendees as prospects or moving them into a pipeline stage — appears as an Approval you can accept or dismiss without leaving your email. It removes the gap between running a webinar and acting on it, so high-intent attendees reach your pipeline the same day.

entries.title: Add branded overlays to recorded webinars, clips and podcast episodes
entries.summary: Organizers can now burn on-brand overlays onto recorded webinars, session videos, clips and video-podcast episodes from the **Event Content Lab** show. Six overlay elements are available per template — **Rundown** (auto-generated chapters with the current chapter highlighted), **Countdown** (time remaining), **Name plates** (speaker name when a tagged speaker begins a turn), **Topic banner** (current chapter or fixed text), **Ticker** (scrolling bottom line) and **Captions** (word-by-word with the spoken word highlighted). Three built-in templates (**Broadcast**, **Lower third**, **Video podcast**) are included per brand kit, and up to 12 custom templates can be saved. Rendered videos appear as **branded_video** items under the source recording or clip.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable branded video overlays; then Marketing → Shows → [Show] → Episode → Add overlay

entries.use_case: Marketing teams that repurpose webinar recordings and podcast episodes can apply a branded overlay — chapters, captions, speaker name plates and a ticker — in a single render pass, so every video clip looks polished and on-brand without a separate video editor.

cs_action.note: API and job infrastructure are live; MCP and UI PRs are follow-ups. Enable per org once the UI is shipped.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to make their recorded webinars or podcast episodes look more polished or on-brand before sharing or publishing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using the Event Content Lab show feature in Marketing who produce regular webinar recordings, clips or video-podcast episodes.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Shows → [Show] → Episode → Add overlay (once UI PR ships)
internal.gotchas: This PR is API-only; the MCP and UI PRs are separate follow-ups. Renders can take up to 3 hours for long videos. Name plates only appear when speakers are tagged as contacts on the recording. Public API docs are not yet updated.
internal.talk_track: You can now burn your brand kit — chapters, captions, speaker names and a scrolling ticker — directly onto any recorded webinar or podcast episode, and download the finished video straight from Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The guide at /sessionboard-marketing/shows/branded-video-overlays does not yet exist and should be created to document the six overlay elements, the three built-in templates, how to create custom templates in a brand kit, how to apply an overlay to a recording or clip, and how to track render status.
draft.why_use_it: Branded video overlays let you publish recordings, clips and podcast episodes that carry your visual identity — logo, fonts, brand colours — along with dynamic elements like auto-generated chapter rundowns, live captions and speaker name plates. Every text colour is automatically checked for contrast against its background so the result meets accessibility standards. Because the render runs entirely inside Sessionboard, you get a finished, downloadable video without leaving the platform or opening a separate editing tool.

entries.title: Apps: connect Google Drive and import folders into Media
entries.summary: A **Google Drive** card is now in the **Apps** catalog under the **Media** category. Once connected, organizers can import Drive folders directly into Media. The connector is visible only to staff until Google completes scope verification.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Google Drive; then Apps → Media → Google Drive → Connect

entries.use_case: Teams that store session recordings or marketing assets in Google Drive can connect their Drive and pull folders straight into Media, removing the need to download and re-upload files manually.

cs_action.note: The connector is staff-only until Google verifies the Drive OAuth scope. Do not surface to customers until the verification is complete.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer stores recordings or session assets in Google Drive and wants to import them into Media without manual downloads.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using Media who also manage content in Google Drive.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Media → Google Drive (visible to staff only until Google scope verification)
internal.gotchas: The catalog entry is live in the UI but the API marks the connector staff-only via catalog-status; customers will not see it until Google verifies the Drive scope.
internal.talk_track: Once Google verifies the scope, you will be able to connect your Drive and import folders directly into Media — no more downloading and re-uploading files.

draft.docs_gap: No guide currently covers the Google Drive integration; a new guide should document how to connect Google Drive, which OAuth scopes are required, and how to import Drive folders into Media.
draft.why_use_it: The Google Drive integration lets you bring folders from your Drive directly into Sessionboard Media, keeping your recordings and assets in one place without manual file transfers. Connect once and import the folders your team already organises in Drive, so content is ready to clip, share or publish without leaving Sessionboard.

entries.title: Agent Sites: build tour listings and per-stop field-event pages by chat
entries.summary: An AI assistant can now build a **tour listing** (a page showing all stops with dates, cities and a request-a-seat link) and a **per-stop field-event page** (hero, key facts, who's in the room, hosts, venue, agenda and registration form) through the agent-sites harness. Every live element — seat counts, waitlist state, attendee-directory counts by organisation type, and the registration form with required questions — is drawn from live event data the assistant already knows about.

where.path: Ask → Sites → build a tour listing or field-event page

entries.use_case: Teams running a field-event tour can ask their AI assistant to generate a public listing of all stops and a dedicated page per stop — complete with live seat counts, waitlist status, an attendee-directory breakdown by organisation type, and a registration form — without writing any HTML or configuring a site builder manually.

cs_action.note: Customers running field-event tours who want a public listing and per-stop pages are the primary audience; walk them through asking the assistant to build the site.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a field-event tour asks how to publish a public stop listing or individual event pages without a web team.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Field Events (beta) who also have agent-sites access and run multi-stop tours.
internal.staff_path: Ask → describe the tour listing or field-event page you want
internal.gotchas: The attendee-directory 'who's in the room' counts only include people who have opted into the directory (directory_listed = true); names are never exposed. The registration form will be refused if a required question is omitted. Published agent sites are now correctly marked indexable; draft and sandbox sites remain noindex.
internal.talk_track: If you run a tour of field events, your AI assistant can now build the public listing and each stop's page for you — live seat counts, waitlist, who's in the room by org type, and the registration form all come from your event data automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The /skills/sites guide should add a section covering tour listings and field-event page kinds, including the tour: binding syntax, the in_the_room data element, and how the registration form's required-question validation works.
draft.why_use_it: The Sites skill lets you describe a page in plain language and have your AI assistant build, populate and publish it for you. For field-event tours it handles the full public surface: a listing of every stop with dates and request-a-seat links, and a per-stop page with the hero, key facts, who's in the room, hosts, venue, agenda and registration form. Pages are generated from live event data, so seat counts, waitlist state and attendee-directory figures stay accurate without manual updates.

entries.title: Reports & Dashboards: clearer errors, safer format patterns, and fixed custom-field aliases with quotes
entries.summary: Four user-visible changes ship together as part of a security hardening pass on the report engine. (1) Database error text in reports, dashboards, shared views and the query log is replaced by a short, readable hint. (2) A `FORMAT_DATE` or `DATE_RANGE` pattern outside the allowed character set now returns a clear `invalid_format_pattern` error instead of a cryptic message. (3) Widget, dashboard and scheduled-report errors that do not come from the query engine show fixed text instead of raw internal messages. (4) A custom field whose display name contains a double-quote (`"`) now works correctly as a column alias; previously it caused a SQL error.

where.path: Reports → Report Builder / Dashboards / Shared report links

entries.use_case: Organizers who use custom date-format patterns in SbQL queries, or who have custom fields with special characters in their names, will see accurate errors and correct results instead of opaque SQL failures. Anyone who shared a dashboard or report link will no longer see raw database error text if a query fails.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that a report or dashboard previously showed a Postgres error message, or that a column for a custom field with a quote in its name was broken.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Report Builder or SbQL with FORMAT_DATE / DATE_RANGE patterns, custom fields whose names include a double-quote, or shared dashboard links.
internal.staff_path: Reports → Report Builder or Dashboards → run a query that fails
internal.gotchas: All 11 distinct format patterns found in production pass the new allow-list. The only patterns now rejected are those containing a single-quote, backslash, semicolon, comment markers or NUL — none of which appeared in any saved query. The error_type field on API responses is unchanged, so MCP server and UI integrations are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: Error messages from reports and dashboards are now short and readable. If a date-format pattern uses a disallowed character, you get a clear invalid_format_pattern error. Custom fields with a double-quote in their name now work as report columns.

draft.docs_gap: The SbQL reference should document the allowed character set for FORMAT_DATE / DATE_RANGE patterns and list the new invalid_format_pattern error code.
draft.why_use_it: The Report Builder and SbQL let you query sessions, speakers, contacts and registrations with full control over columns, filters, grouping and date formatting. Errors surface as structured codes so you can fix a query without reading database internals, and results are safe to share with colleagues via dashboard links or scheduled reports.

entries.title: Rich-text fields in submissions, speaker bios and embeds are now sanitized
entries.summary: Script tags, event-handler attributes (`on*=`), and other disallowed HTML are now stripped from rich-text answers and speaker **About / Bio** fields at both write time and read time, regardless of how the field type was declared on submission. Ordinary formatting — bold, links, lists, tables — is unchanged. **Program Site** pages and agenda embeds now serve the sanitized value for all rich-text fields.

where.path: Sessions → Submission Forms; Portals → Speaker portal; Sites → Program Site; Sessions → Embeds

entries.use_case: Any event that collects rich-text answers or speaker bios through public forms can be confident that script tags and handler attributes submitted by bad actors are discarded before the content reaches a Site page, embed, or portal — no configuration required.

cs_action.note: Embed stale cache key moves to embed-stale-v4; each embed rebuilds cold once after deploy. The 60-minute response cache expires on its own within an hour, or admins can purge per embed. Watch rebuild locks (RCA-US-20261118-1625 context). Embeds PROD publish is a manual step that must ship with this release (embeds PR #146).

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that formatted content in a bio, abstract or awards answer looks different after the release, or asks why certain HTML tags are no longer appearing in their embed or Site output.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — this is a security fix applied to every event and org that uses rich-text fields on public forms, speaker portals, Sites or embeds.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Submission Forms (rich-text fields); Portals → speaker portal bio; Sites → Program Site; Sessions → Embeds
internal.gotchas: US prod data audit found 7 affected rows in non-internal orgs (all Module_Field_Values); EU had 189 allow-listed <iframe> embeds with zero script/handler matches. ME replica was unreachable at audit time. A backfill of stored values is optional — the read-side sanitization makes existing rows safe without a migration. The one test failure (embed/utils/get-async-data-with-stale.test.js) pre-exists on main and is unrelated.
internal.talk_track: Rich-text answers and speaker bios submitted through public forms are now sanitized on both save and display, so script tags and handler attributes are discarded automatically. Normal formatting is completely unaffected.

draft.docs_gap: The Embeds guide should note that rich-text field values served to V1 widgets and the plain embed payload are sanitized with the platform allow-list, and that the embed cache key changed to embed-stale-v4 in November 2026.

entries.title: Reviewers no longer see Ask panel errors or organizer content
entries.summary: Reviewers whose only access is **My Reviews** no longer see a red "Request failed" error toast on every page load, and the **Ask** panel no longer auto-opens with organizer-oriented content (such as links to Dashboard, Apps, Automations and Agents) that they cannot use.
entries.use_case: Reviewers landing on My Reviews no longer encounter a confusing error toast or an AI panel filled with organizer setup prompts they have no access to, giving them a clean, distraction-free experience.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that reviewers were seeing 'Request failed' toasts or the Ask panel opening with organizer content on My Reviews.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using review plans where reviewers have restricted access (My Reviews only).
internal.gotchas: Reviewers still have access to the evaluator assistant on the Program Site; only the organizer-facing Ask panel and daily brief are suppressed.
internal.talk_track: Reviewers now get a clean My Reviews page with no error messages or out-of-place AI prompts.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that reviewers with My Reviews-only access do not see the Ask panel or receive daily briefs.
